Rules and limits, explained Employee Provident Fund Organisation: EPF subscribers are allowed to withdraw up to 100% of their eligible provident fund balance, with certain conditions. Here are the new rules and top FAQs explained… Jocelyn Fernandes Published 31 Oct 2026, 02:53 PM IST Prefer Livemint on Google Employee Provident Fund Organisation: EPF subscribers can partially withdraw up to 100% of their eligible PF balance or 75% of total balance under certain conditions. ( AI generated image for representational purposes only ) AI Quick Read Subscribers of the Employee Provident Fund Organisation ( EPFO ) are now allowed to withdraw the maximum eligible funds, including the employee and employer shares, as per a Labour Ministry release last year. The EPFO's Central Board of Trustees ( CBT ) approved the simplified withdrawal rules, which allow EPF members to access up to 75% of their total corpus, with mandatory requirement to keep at least 25% of the funds untouched as a buffer. Can you withdraw full EPF funds? Rules explained EPFO members are allowed to withdraw up to 100% of eligible funds i.e. 75% of their provident fund balance, after setting aside required minimum balance. Partial withdrawal provisions were simplified in October last year by merging 13 provisions into the three categories — Essential needs, housing related needs and special circumstances. Also Read | Gold, silver rates today Bangalore 31 Oct: Latest price movement for investors The special circumstances category includes provision for job loss, where you can claim up to 75% immediate withdrawal and the remaining 25% after two months of unemployment. There are three types of withdrawal claims allowed, and you will be required to state the reason why you want to make a withdrawal. Types of withdrawals allowed are as specified below: New Rules on EPF Advances Category I: Essential Needs Illness (self and family) No limit Education (self and family) Up to 10 times during membership Marriage (self and family) Up to 5 times during membership Category II: Housing related needs Purchase of house / flat / site Up to 5 times during membership Construction of house Up to 5 times during membership Repayment of home loan Up to 5 times during membership Renovation / alteration / improvement Up to 5 times during membership Category III: Special circumstances Special circumstances as notified by the Central Board, EPF Up to 2 times in a financial year Which forms to use for EPF partial, withdrawal claim? Partial withdrawal of EPF funds allows members to claim non-refundable advances while actively employed. To make this claim, you will have to fill and submit Form 31. Further, the new rules also extend the period to avail early withdrawal / premature final settlement of EPF from the existing two months to 12 months; and final pension withdrawal from two months to 36 months. The final provident fund settlement requires submission of Form 19. Under this, you can claim withdrawal of your full PF balance (inclusive of employee share, employer share, and interest earned). Also Read | 5 key money changes from 1 November: Life certificate, ITR, GST, bank charges When are members eligible for 100% PF, pension? Subscribers only become eligible for 100% funds withdrawal once they have retired or resigned and remained continuously unemployed for at least two months i.e. 60 days. For pension, at time of retirement, you can choose to either withdraw amount in full or maintain annuity in EPS by availing a Scheme Certificat e. Submitting Form 10C allows you to withdraw accumulated pension as a lumpsum, if your total continuous service is less than 10 years. Beyond 10 years, you must secure a Scheme Certificate and await monthly pension payouts at age 58. How long does PF withdrawal claim take? Online claims for members who have completed full KYC take between three to seven working days, according to the FAQ website. Meanwhile, auto-mode eligible claims take 72 hours, it said. And offline physical claims submitted to EPFO office can take up to 20 working days. Once successfully submitted, claims are generally approved and settled (credited to bank account) within seven to 15 working days. You will receive an SMS alert at every stage of the process — submitted, approved, and disbursed. Disclaimer: This story is for educational purposes only.
